title: PixelForge loadout
description: One named equipment pool -- a class. A loadout names WHICH attachment layers a class offers per slot; it holds no pixels and references no hero, because an attachment layer is tone-independent and stacks onto any body. That is why loadouts live once at the export root rather than once per hero. A slot may offer several stems: this is a pool a consumer picks from per character, not a fixed kit. The sheets themselves live under attachments/<slot>/<stem>.webp and are described by the run manifest. Validate against the copy of this schema shipped in the SAME folder.

$schema.description: Relative path to the schema copied beside this file. Loadouts sit one directory down, so this is normally ../pixelforge-loadouts-v1.json.

schemaVersion.description: Semantic version of this loadout format, and the single place it is declared. Policy matches the run manifest: an optional property added at an open object is a MINOR bump; a change to the closed slots object, or a removed, retyped or newly required property, mints a new $id, a new -vN filename and a new generated type.

class.description: The slugged class name the user typed, such as ranger. Matches this file's own name and its row in classes.csv.

assignedInRun.description: The run that last wrote this loadout. Loadouts are keyed by name and rewritten whole, so unlike a hero number this IS recency.

stems.description: The attachment stems this class offers for one slot, such as hair1 and hair7. Each names a file at attachments/<slot>/<stem>.webp. More than one means the class offers a choice, not that it wears several at once -- a slot draws at most one layer.

slots.description: Equipment by slot. A slot this class does not use is ABSENT rather than an empty array. Closed to extra properties, and deliberately narrower than the run manifest's slots object: bottom, top and head are the body -- they make a hero, not a loadout -- so only the seven optional slots appear here. Property spellings match the run manifest's slots object so one reader serves both.
